title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 1.51 (versions follow prime numbers; 151 after 149): she learns to draw every letter she meets. Her own dot alphabet had only A-Z, 0-9 and '?'; every other character typed to her showed as an empty cell. Instead of a hand-made alphabet (set aside at the author's request), she now learns: when she meets a character she cannot draw, she looks it up in her book of letters (GNU Unifont 18.0.01, free, kept in her house), copies its drawing into her own alphabet file and draws it from then on, at half size. She keeps only what she meets and remembers it when born again; a character missing from the book is kept as a frame. Tested with '¡Hola! papá ñandú 🌱 ∑ 中': eight characters learned, drawn, and remembered after a new birth. Stated limits: she copies rather than invents shapes; fine drawings lose detail at half size; learned letters vary in width; the 8.3 MB book of letters is not in the repository. The kernel is unchanged since 1.39. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v1.51: Luma aprende a dibujar cada letra que se encuentra, copiándola de un libro de letras libre. Prototipo de investigación.
